ei.title: Life Is a Journey to Be Experienced

questions.passage: I was fond of swimming. One summer day, I was watching an Olympic swimming event on TV. The gold medalist ⓐ looked fantastic, and I wanted to be just like him. I asked my parents if I could learn to swim. They approved and said, "Yes." Swimming was difficult at first, but after a year, I became a good swimmer. I felt tired but happy when I was out of breath after every practice. As I practiced more, my times got better and better. One day, my coach suggested that I ⓑ entered a competition. He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength through weight training. The training was ⓒ demanding, leaving me ⓓ exhausted at times. Whenever I felt this way, I told myself, "No pain, no ⓔ gain."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] my coach suggested that I entered a competition. [해석] 코치가 나에게 시합에 나가라고 제안했다. suggest(제안하다)는 당위·제안을 나타내는 동사로, that절에서 should + 동사원형 또는 동사원형을 사용해야 합니다. entered(과거형)는 어법에 맞지 않으며, enter(동사원형)로 바꿔야 합니다.
det.correct:
ⓐ looked: 2형식 감각동사 look + 형용사 보어(fantastic) → 주격보어 구문 ✅
ⓑ entered: suggest that + S + (should) 동사원형 → entered(과거형) ❌ → enter가 되어야 합니다
ⓒ demanding: 주어 The training의 보어, '힘든'이라는 능동적 의미의 현재분사 ✅
ⓓ exhausted: 분사구문 leaving me exhausted — me(사람)의 감정 → 과거분사 ✅
ⓔ gain: No pain, no gain(고진감래) — gain(명사: 얻음) ✅
det.tip: 🔑 제안·요구·명령·주장 동사 + that절: (should) 동사원형 — suggest / recommend / insist / demand + that + S + (should) + 동사원형. 비교: suggest가 '암시하다' 의미일 때는 직설법 사용

questions.passage: I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I (A) [take / taking] on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. So, I decided to do it. I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more confident. On the day of the performance, I got anxious and my mind (B) [went / was gone] blank just before I stepped on the stage. My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and (C) [encouraged / encouraging] me.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] (A) suggest that I take → 제안동사 + that + 동사원형. (B) my mind went blank → go + 형용사(상태변화). (C) tapped and encouraged → 병렬구조(과거+과거). [해석] (A) 선생님이 작은 역할을 맡으라고 제안했다 (B) 머릿속이 하얘졌다 (C) 어깨를 두드리며 격려했다
det.correct:
① take/went/encouraged: suggest that+동사원형 ✅, go blank(상태변화) ✅, tapped and encouraged 병렬 ✅ → 정답
② take/was gone/encouraging: was gone blank 비문 ❌, 병렬 위반 ❌
③ taking/went/encouraged: suggest that+taking 불가 ❌
④ taking/was gone/encouraged: (A) ❌, (B) ❌
⑤ taking/went/encouraging: (A) ❌, (C) 병렬 위반 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 go + 형용사: 상태 변화 — go blank(하얘지다), go wrong(잘못되다), go bad(상하다). 🔑 병렬 구조: A and B = 같은 문법 형태 → tapped(과거) and encouraged(과거)

questions.passage: When Steve Jobs was a college student, he did not know ⓐ what he wanted to do in the future. He felt uncertain about how the normal classes he was required to take could help him figure out what to do with his life. He decided to start ⓑ checking out things that seemed interesting to him. One day, he was walking around the college grounds and a poster caught his eye. He became fascinated with the art of ⓒ producing beautiful handwriting, also known as calligraphy. He gained an understanding of letter styles and learned to adjust the spacing between various combinations of letters. At that time, he did not expect that learning it would be useful or applicable ⓓ for his life in the future.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] applicable for his life → 원문은 applicable to. [해석] 미래에 자신의 삶에 적용 가능할 것이라고. applicable은 전치사 to와 함께 써야 합니다. for는 어법 오류입니다.
det.correct:
ⓐ what he wanted to do: 간접의문문(의문사+S+V 어순) → what(목적어)+he(S)+wanted to do(V) ✅
ⓑ checking out: start + v-ing / to-v 둘 다 가능 ✅
ⓒ producing: the art of + v-ing(동명사) ✅
ⓓ applicable for: applicable은 전치사 to와 함께 → applicable to ❌ 정답
det.tip: 🔑 applicable to (○) / applicable for (✕). apply to(~에 적용되다), be applicable to(~에 적용 가능한). 비교: available for, suitable for. 🔑 간접의문문 어순: 의문사 + S + V

questions.passage: One day, I saw a poster advertising the city's landscape design contest. The instant I saw it, I got interested. After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging and (A) [decorating / destroying] outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was (B) [impressive / depressive] because the arrangement of plants and structures can transform a space. This (C) [inspired / expired] me to think about becoming a landscape architect.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] arranging and decorating / impressive / inspired [해석] 야외 공간을 배치하고 꾸미다 / 인상적이었다 / 영감을 주었다
det.correct:
① decorating/impressive/inspired: 꾸미다/인상적/영감 → 모두 적절 ✅ 정답
② depressive(우울한) ❌, expired(만료된) ❌
③ destroying(파괴하다) 부적절 ❌
④ destroying ❌, depressive ❌
⑤ expired(만료된) ❌
det.tip: 🔑 inspire ≈ motivate ≈ encourage ↔ discourage. inspire(영감) vs expire(만료) — 접두사 in-(안으로) vs ex-(밖으로). impressive(인상적) ↔ depressive(우울한)

questions.passage: Changes in your interests and preferences are completely ① natural. Try to accept this process and keep an open mind. Exploring new things can sometimes lead to ② valuable experiences which will help shape your future. I myself tried many different things before I finally became an editor because I enjoyed writing. Thanks to these many interests, I can write articles about math and science, speak ③ confidently in front of an audience, and ④ intensify my stress by swimming. Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a ⑤ waste of time.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.ref: [원문] relieve my stress by swimming → 수영으로 스트레스를 완화하다. intensify(강화하다)는 원문 relieve(완화하다)의 반의어로 문맥에 부적절합니다.
det.correct:
① natural: 변화가 자연스러운 것 ✅
② valuable: 가치 있는 경험 ✅
③ confidently: 자신 있게 말하다 ✅
④ intensify: 스트레스를 강화? → 원문은 relieve(완화) ❌ 정답
⑤ waste: 시간 낭비가 아니다 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 relieve(완화하다) ≈ ease ≈ alleviate ↔ intensify(강화하다) ≈ worsen ≈ aggravate. 반의어 함정: 원문 핵심 어휘를 반의어로 교체 → 문맥 흐름(긍정/부정) 파악이 핵심

questions.passage: He became ① fascinated with the art of producing beautiful handwriting, also known as calligraphy, and decided to attend a calligraphy class. He gained an understanding of letter styles and learned to adjust the ② spacing between various combinations of letters. At that time, he did not expect that learning it would be useful or ③ applicable to his life in the future. However, later when he developed his own computer operating system, he ④ eliminated what he learned from that class into designing the system. As a result, he developed his own computer system with ⑤ visually appealing letter styles.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.ref: [원문] incorporated what he learned into designing the system [해석] 배운 것을 시스템 디자인에 통합했다. eliminated(제거하다)는 원문 incorporated(통합하다)의 반의어.
det.correct:
① fascinated: 매료된 ✅
② spacing: 간격 ✅
③ applicable: 적용 가능한 ✅
④ eliminated: 제거하다 → 원문은 incorporated(통합하다) ❌ 정답
⑤ visually: 시각적으로 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 incorporate A into B(A를 B에 통합) ≈ integrate ≈ include ↔ eliminate(제거) ≈ remove ≈ exclude. 어원: incorporate = in(안으로)+corpus(몸)

questions.passage: Can you guess what my friends do now? Are they a swimmer? An actor? A landscape architect? A novelist? Actually, all four of these people are me! I currently work as a magazine editor. As you can see, my preferences have changed over the years as I was exposed to new experiences. Every time my interest changed, I was worried about what I was going to become in the future. Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept this process and keep an open mind. Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences which will help shape your future.
questions.stem: 이 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences which will help shape your future. [해석] 새로운 것을 탐구하는 것은 미래를 형성하는 데 도움이 되는 가치 있는 경험으로 이어질 수 있다.
det.correct:
① 일찍 하나의 직업 선택의 중요성 → 다양한 경험 권장과 반대 ❌
② 다양한 경험이 미래를 형성하는 데 가치 있다 → 핵심 주제 ✅ 정답
③ 장기 취미 유지의 어려움 → 초점 아님 ❌
④ 꿈의 직업 찾기 전략 → 구체적 전략보다 경험의 가치 ❌
⑤ 관심사 변경의 부정적 영향 → 글은 변화를 긍정적으로 묘사 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 주제 찾기: 글의 마지막 부분(주제문)에 핵심 메시지 집중. 키워드: valuable experiences, shape your future, keep an open mind

ch: the importance of choosing a single career early in life
the value of diverse experiences in shaping one's future
the difficulty of maintaining long-term hobbies
the best strategies for finding a dream job
the negative effects of changing interests frequently

questions.passage: When Steve Jobs was a college student, he did not know what he wanted to do in the future. He felt uncertain about how the normal classes he was required to take could help him figure out what to do with his life. He decided to start checking out things that seemed interesting to him. He became fascinated with calligraphy and decided to attend a calligraphy class. At that time, he did not expect that learning it would be useful or applicable to his life in the future. However, later when he developed his own computer operating system, he incorporated what he learned from that class into designing the system. His innovative incorporation of calligraphy into the world of technology has inspired many other corporations' computer system designs.
questions.stem: 이 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] His innovative incorporation of calligraphy into the world of technology, which started from his personal interest, has inspired many. [해석] 개인적 관심에서 시작된 서예의 기술 세계 통합이 많은 이들에게 영감을 주었다.
det.correct:
① 서예의 달인 → 서예 자체가 핵심이 아님 ❌
② 호기심이 혁신으로 이어진 과정 → curiosity→calligraphy→computer design ✅ 정답
③ 디지털 시대 손글씨 쇠퇴 → 주제 아님 ❌
④ 대학 수업이 쓸모없는 이유 → 주제 아님 ❌
⑤ 기술 vs 예술 싸움 → 대립이 아닌 융합 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 제목 = 주제를 함축적으로 표현. 핵심 흐름: curiosity → calligraphy class → computer design innovation

ch: Steve Jobs: The Master of Calligraphy
The Decline of Handwriting in the Digital Age
Technology vs. Art: A Never-ending Battle

questions.passage: Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time. Your school days are a time of self-discovery and personal growth. As you spend each day wisely, you will be able to figure out what kind of person you are and what you enjoy doing. Do not attempt to define yourself in just one way as you undergo this process. Be flexible. Remember that your potential is limitless. At that time, he did not expect that learning it would be useful or applicable to his life in the future. However, later when he developed his own computer operating system, he incorporated what he learned from that class into designing the system.
questions.stem: 이 글이 시사하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time. / he did not expect... However, he incorporated what he learned. [해석] 다양한 경험은 시간 낭비가 아니다. 예상치 못한 학습이 미래 성취의 토대가 되었다.
det.correct:
① 일찍 직업 계획해야 성공 → 유연함 강조와 반대 ❌
② 예상치 못한 경험이 미래 성취의 토대 → Jobs의 서예+Minji의 경험 = 핵심 시사점 ✅ 정답
③ 학업 성적이 가장 중요 → 언급 없음 ❌
④ 관심사 변경을 피해야 한다 → 반대 ❌
⑤ 기술 분야만 창의성 중요 → 모든 분야 경험 가치 강조 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 시사점 = 직접 언급되지 않은 깊은 교훈. did not expect + applicable → incorporated → 예상 못 한 경험 = 미래 성취

questions.passage: Hi, everyone. My name is Minji Song, and I am the editor of an online teen magazine, Teens Today. I am honored to have been asked to give a talk. Many of our high school student subscribers send me messages with concerns about their future. So today, I will talk about the value of experiences in making a better future. For this talk, I asked my old friends to write down stories about what they experienced when they were younger.
questions.stem: Minji Song에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I am the editor of an online teen magazine, Teens Today. [해석] 나는 온라인 청소년 잡지 Teens Today의 편집자이다.
det.correct:
① 고등학생이다 → 잡지 편집자 ❌
② 인쇄 신문 편집 → online magazine ❌
③ 온라인 청소년 잡지에서 일한다 → 일치 ✅ 정답
④ 구독자가 대학생 → high school student subscribers ❌
⑤ Minji가 이야기를 작성 → 친구들에게 써 달라고 부탁 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 일치 문제: 선지 키워드를 지문에서 정확히 대조. 함정: printed vs online, newspaper vs magazine, wrote vs asked to write

This is because landscape architects must calculate the dimensions and slopes of land as well as thoroughly examine environmental factors such as soil, air, and climate. det.ref: [원문] I was not good at either subject at the time [해석] 그 당시 두 과목 모두 잘하지 못했다. '이미 뛰어났다'는 내용과 불일치.
det.correct:
① 조경 건축가가 되고 싶었다 → 일치 ✅
② 수학·과학 지식 필요 → 일치 ✅
③ 환경 요인 고려 → 일치 ✅

I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time. I felt a sense of relief when I wrote what I wanted to do after leaving the hospital. That evening, I asked my mother to buy me a notebook. As I filled page after page, I realized that writing was more than just ______________. As the years passed, my passion for writing grew stronger.

det.ref: [원문] writing was more than just a way to kill time. [해석] 글쓰기가 단지 시간을 때우는 방법 이상이라는 것을 깨달았다.

questions.passage:
주어진 글: When Steve Jobs was a college student, he did not know what he wanted to do in the future. He felt uncertain about how the normal classes he was required to take could help him figure out what to do with his life.

(A) He became fascinated with the art of producing beautiful handwriting, also known as calligraphy, and decided to attend a calligraphy class.
(B) He decided to start checking out things that seemed interesting to him. One day, he was walking around the college grounds and a poster caught his eye. The handwritten letters on every poster were elegant and beautiful.
(C) He gained an understanding of letter styles and learned to adjust the spacing between various combinations of letters. However, later he incorporated what he learned into designing his computer operating system.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [해석] 주어진 글: 미래를 몰랐다 → (B) 흥미로운 것 찾기 시작 → 포스터 발견 → (A) 서예에 매료 → 수업 수강 → (C) 글자 스타일 학습 → 컴퓨터에 적용
det.correct:
① (A)-(B)-(C): 먼저 매료 후 찾기? 역전 ❌
② (A)-(C)-(B): 논리 불가 ❌
③ (B)-(A)-(C): 찾기→매료→학습→적용 ✅ 정답
④ (B)-(C)-(A): 학습 후 매료? 역순 ❌
⑤ (C)-(A)-(B): 완전 역전 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 순서배열: 지시어·연결사·시간 흐름 추적. decided to start(B) → fascinated(A) → gained understanding(C). also known as: ~라고도 알려진

questions.passage: I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. So, I decided to do it. I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more confident. On the day of the performance, I got anxious and my mind went blank just before I stepped on the stage. My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and encouraged me. Thanks to this, I was able to perform my lines perfectly.

det.correct: ✅ 정답: confidence — gained(동사)+명사 구조. 보기 단어 confidence 그대로 활용(이미 명사형). ❌ confident(형용사), confidently(부사)는 gained 뒤에 부적절
det.tip: 🔑 confident(형용사) → confidence(명사) → confidently(부사). gain confidence = 자신감을 얻다. 요약형: 보기 단어의 적절한 품사 확인

det.ref: [원문] are still widely used. [해석] 여전히 널리 사용된다. are + 부사(widely) + p.p.(used) = 수동태. 주어(letters)가 사용되는 대상이므로 수동태 필수.
det.correct: ✅ used — be + p.p. 수동태. ❌ use(원형: are+use 비문), using(능동 진행형: 의미 부적절), useful(형용사: 원문과 다름)
det.tip: 🔑 수동태: be + p.p. — are used(사용된다). 부사 위치: be + 부사 + p.p. → are widely used. 능동: People use them / 수동: They are used.
